title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(土田義郎研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Tsuchida Yoshio)
educationalGoal: Architecture and cities are required to have various functions for human life. There, environmental comfort is important. The fundamental goal of the lab is to know the psychological response to the physical environment. In this subject, we study the psychological system of human environmental recognition and evaluation. The laboratory aims to contribute to the construction of architectural and urban spaces.
advice: * Project flow [1] Rewrite the proposal created during the third grade. Make an oral presentation in the seminar and submit the revised proposal. [2] To obtain the necessary knowledge for the project, abstract related documents. [3] Conduct surveys and experiments based on proposals. Use the method appropriate for the purpose of the project. [4] Hold an interim report meeting twice a year. Create a summary paper in the prescribed format. And give an oral presentation. [5] Submit a project report and an outline on a fixed date, and give a presentation outside the university at a public review board. * Unlike general lectures and experiments, there is no fixed methodology. It is necessary to devise original ideas after carefully conducting past case studies. I want you to always have a spirit of challenge. * Some activities are required during the spring break. If the direction is not fixed by that time, the activities will be delayed later and it will be difficult to reach the ideal level.
requiredKnowledge: Students are assumed to have a knowledge of environmental engineering.

activityGoals.body: Students can review previous research relevant to a project theme.
Students can conceive an experiment, survey, and analysis necessary to move the research forward.
Students can correctly explain actual conditions and phenomena related to the environment & energy consumption.
Students can create and display suitable charts to aid in explanations to third parties.
Students can create an appropriate project report.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Students review previous research relevant to a project theme crossing to two or more scientific fields. (2) Students conceive an experiment, survey, and analysis required to move the research forward and clarify the originality of their research. (3) Students can correctly explain the actual conditions and phenomena related to the thermal environment and primary energy consumption based on usage. (4) Students create and display suitable and attractive charts to the audience in a society presentation. (5) Students create appropriate project reports.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Students review previous research relevant to a project theme. (2) Students conceive an experiment, survey, and analysis required to move the research forward. (3) Students can correctly explain the actual conditions and phenomena related to the environment and energy consumption. (4) Students create and display suitable charts for explaining their findings to a third party. (5) Students create appropriate project reports.
